lakes.name: St. Moritzersee
lakes.authority: SEE-INFRA AG measures; Lake Ice Committee reviews; Gemeindevorstand St. Moritz grants the release phases
lakes.notes: Quantitative monitoring starts at 6 cm ice at points across the lake; above 27 cm SEE-INFRA applies for the 'Green Phase'; then a 7,700 kg snow-groomer crash test, after which vehicles up to 3,500 kg are cleared. Ground-penetrating radar used. No public live status page found; contact welcome@see-infra.org.

rules.t: In canton Zürich the shoreline municipalities (Zürichsee: Kantonspolizei/Seepolizei) release or close frozen waters; ice that is not released must not be entered.
In many other Swiss cantons there is no release; lakes are signposted 'Betreten auf eigene Gefahr'.
SLRG minimum clear-ice thickness: 5 cm for individuals, 7-8 cm for a small crowd, 10-12 cm for a large crowd, 15 cm for a 1 t vehicle.
src: SLRG / Röthlisberger, Tragverhalten von Eis (via SLF)

rules.t: Count snow-ice (white, bubbly) at only half its measured thickness.
bfu: on open natural ice follow the 6 SLRG ice rules.
DLRG: at least 15 cm on standing water and 20 cm on flowing water; use only officially released and supervised ice; never go alone.
DLRG ice rules: ask the official authority whether the ice is thick enough; stay off ice during the first cold days.
In Bavaria municipalities may ban entering or driving on ice surfaces by ordinance (LStVG Art. 27); ask the local Gemeinde.
Upper Austrian civil protection: enter ice only at 15 cm on standing and 20 cm on flowing water.
In Austria release is usually by local clubs and covers only marked areas, not whole lakes.
Without extensive ice experience, stay off ice thinner than 10 cm.
Clear ice must be at least 5-10 cm to carry a walking person; slush ice has about half the strength; in spring even 20-30 cm may not hold.
Red Cross: 15 cm for walking/skating in small groups, 20 cm for larger groups, 25 cm for snowmobiles/ATVs; check with local authorities.
Minnesota DNR (new clear ice): under 4 in stay off; 4 in on foot; 5-7 in snowmobile; 9-10 in small car; double for white ice. The DNR does not measure lake ice.
French Alps/Jura guide: ice should be at least 12 cm to safely carry one person; skating at Lamoura depends on a municipal order.
Flowing water and rivers are much more dangerous than standing water and should generally not be walked on.

model.t: Stefan's law: ice accretion is proportional to the square root of accumulated freezing degree-days (h = alpha * sqrt(AFDD)).

Modified Stefan (Michel 1971): empirical coefficient alpha about 1.4-1.7 cm per sqrt(degC*day) (paper prints 0.014-0.017 in m units); lower values (1.4-1.5) fit snowy winters, higher (1.6-1.7) fit winters with little snow.
Zubov formula (cm): h = -25 + sqrt((25 + h0)^2 + 8 * sum(-T)), useful when no thick snow cover.
Rule of thumb: about 1 inch of ice per 15 Fahrenheit freezing degree-days with light wind, no snow and clear skies; roughly half that rate with heavy snow and calm overcast conditions.

Freeze-over thresholds (Kältesumme = sum of negative daily mean temps): Pfäffikersee 120, Greifensee 130, Bielersee 170, Hallwilersee 180, Sempachersee 230, Zürichsee ~300, Bodensee 370; frozen does not mean load-bearing.
Load capacity: P (kg) = 5 * h^2 with h in cm, adequate for ice thicker than 5 cm (10 cm -> 500 kg).
